demand.question: What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN in one sentence (an IPsec connection between your network and a VPC or transit gateway)? Quote the guide's definitions of the VPN connection, the VPN tunnel, the customer gateway, the customer gateway device and the target gateway.

Does each Site-to-Site VPN connection have two tunnels, and why (redundancy; each tunnel uses a unique public IP address)? What does AWS recommend (configure both tunnels), and what can happen to one tunnel during AWS maintenance or an endpoint replacement?

How does Site-to-Site VPN protect data in transit: IPsec, which IKE versions, which encryption and integrity algorithms and Diffie-Hellman groups can a tunnel use? Does the VPN traffic travel over the internet?

Which tunnel authentication options exist (pre-shared keys, a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority)? Can the pre-shared key be stored in AWS Secrets Manager, and since when (document-history row 2025-05-27)?

Which side initiates the IKE negotiation by default (the customer gateway device), and can AWS initiate it instead? What is the dead peer detection (DPD) timeout default and the default DPD timeout action?

A virtual private gateway attaches to one VPC at a time: quote it. To connect the same VPN to several VPCs, what does AWS recommend (a transit gateway)? Do VPN connections on a transit gateway count against the transit gateway attachment quota?

What does the customer gateway device need (an internet-routable IP address, or a private IP address for a private IP VPN; IKE, IPsec, BGP for dynamic routing)? Can the customer gateway sit behind a NAT device (NAT traversal)?

Maximum bandwidth and packets per second per tunnel: standard tunnel (up to 1.25 Gbps, 140,000 PPS), large bandwidth tunnel (up to 5 Gbps, 400,000 PPS), VPN Concentrator tunnel (up to 100 Mbps, 10,000 PPS). Quote each row of the 'Bandwidth and throughput' table with its header; also the sentence that IPv6 VPNs have the same throughput as IPv4.

Large bandwidth tunnels: which target gateways support them (transit gateway, AWS Cloud WAN; is a virtual private gateway excluded)? Can the tunnel bandwidth of an existing VPN connection be changed (2026-05-06)? Is an accelerated VPN compatible with a large bandwidth tunnel?

How do you get more VPN bandwidth than one tunnel gives: ECMP across several VPN tunnels on a transit gateway. Quote that ECMP needs dynamic (BGP) routing and is not supported with static routing. Does a virtual private gateway support ECMP across tunnels?

Site-to-Site VPN resource quotas, each row with header and adjustable flag: customer gateways per Region (50), virtual private gateways per Region (5), VPN connections per Region (50), VPN connections per virtual private gateway (10), accelerated VPN connections per Region (10), large bandwidth tunnel connections per Region, VPN Concentrators per Region and per transit gateway, remote sites per VPN Concentrator.

demand.question: Route quotas: dynamic routes from a customer gateway to a VPN on a virtual private gateway (100) and on a transit gateway (1,000); routes advertised to the customer gateway from a virtual private gateway (1,000) and from a transit gateway (5,000); static routes (100). Each row with its header.
Maximum transmission unit of a Site-to-Site VPN (1446 bytes; MSS 1406 bytes). Are jumbo frames supported? Is Path MTU Discovery supported?
Static routing vs dynamic routing (BGP): what each means, which one AWS recommends when the device supports BGP, and what BGP adds (failover between tunnels, route advertisement).

Route priority: when the same prefix is learned over Direct Connect and over a Site-to-Site VPN on a virtual private gateway (or a transit gateway), which path wins? Quote the ordered list (longest prefix first; then static vs propagated; Direct Connect BGP routes before VPN static routes before VPN BGP routes; AS_PATH for BGP).

How do VPN routes reach the VPC route table (route propagation from the virtual private gateway, or a static route to the virtual private gateway)? Reuse vpc-route-propagation-from-vgw if it fits; add the VPN guide sentence.

Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN: what it does (AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic from the on-premises network to the nearest AWS edge location), which target gateway it requires (transit gateway only, not a virtual private gateway), whether an existing VPN can be converted, and whether it works over a public Direct Connect virtual interface.

AWS VPN CloudHub: what it is (hub-and-spoke between several remote sites through one virtual private gateway), what it requires (BGP, a unique ASN per site, non-overlapping ranges), and whether it uses the internet.
Redundant VPN connections: how to protect against the loss of the customer gateway device (a second customer gateway device and a second VPN connection; dynamic routing for automatic failover).

Private IP VPN over Direct Connect: what it is (IPsec VPN with private IP addresses over a Direct Connect transit virtual interface), what it requires (a transit gateway and a Direct Connect gateway), and why use it (encrypt Direct Connect traffic without public IP addresses).

VPN Concentrator: what it is (many small remote sites on one attachment of a transit gateway or Cloud WAN), its tunnel bandwidth and remote-site quota, and when it became available (2025-11-15 history, 2025-11-19 What's New).

Monitoring: which CloudWatch metrics show tunnel state and data (TunnelState, TunnelDataIn, TunnelDataOut); which logs exist (tunnel activity logs, BGP logs) and where they go (CloudWatch Logs); how AWS Health reports tunnel endpoint replacements.
IPv6: can a VPN carry IPv6 traffic inside the tunnels, and on which target gateways? Can the outer tunnel IP addresses be IPv6 (2025-07-01)?
Software VPN on Amazon EC2 (customer-managed) vs AWS Site-to-Site VPN: who manages high availability and the appliance, and when the whitepaper suggests a software VPN.

Site-to-Site VPN pricing dimensions (no dollar amounts): VPN connection-hour, data transfer out; what an accelerated VPN adds (Global Accelerator fees); whether large bandwidth tunnels and VPN Concentrators have their own hourly charge. What defines a billable connection-hour (reuse vpc-faq-vpn-connection-hour-billing if it fits).
Tunnel endpoint lifecycle control: what it lets you do (schedule AWS maintenance updates of tunnel endpoints). Recognition only.

What is AWS Direct Connect in one sentence (links your internal network to a Direct Connect location over a standard Ethernet fiber-optic cable)? Quote the guide's components: connections, virtual interfaces, and the statement that traffic bypasses internet service providers.

Network requirements: single-mode fiber with the named transceivers, 802.1Q VLAN encapsulation, BGP and BGP MD5 authentication, optional BFD. Where must your router be (at the Direct Connect location, or reached through a partner or network provider)? Does AWS provide the 'last mile' circuit?
Port speeds: dedicated connections (1, 10, 100, 400 Gbps); hosted connections (50 Mbps up to 25 Gbps, list each value). Which hosted speeds only some partners offer (1 Gbps and above).

Dedicated connection vs hosted connection: a dedicated connection is a physical Ethernet port for one customer, requested from AWS; a hosted connection is provisioned by a Direct Connect Partner. Quote both definitions.

Virtual interface quotas: private or public virtual interfaces per dedicated connection (50), transit virtual interfaces per dedicated connection (4), total per dedicated connection (51), virtual interfaces per hosted connection (1), active connections per location per Region per account (10). Each row with header and comment ('cannot be increased').

Ordering a dedicated connection: request, then the Letter of Authorization and Connecting Facility Assignment (LOA-CFA), then the cross connect. How long is an LOA-CFA valid? When do port-hour charges start (connection up, or a fixed number of days after creation)?

Is Direct Connect traffic encrypted by default? Quote 'does not encrypt your traffic that is in transit by default' with its next sentence, and the options the guide names (Site-to-Site VPN over Direct Connect for IPsec, MACsec, the encryption of each service).

MACsec: what it protects (layer 2, from your router to the Direct Connect location, not end to end), which connections support it (dedicated 10, 100, 400 Gbps at selected locations; not hosted connections), cipher suites, and whether it replaces other encryption (FAQ).
Privacy of the path: does Direct Connect traffic stay off the public internet? Quote the guide's 'Internetwork traffic privacy' page and the whitepaper security page.
demand.note: partial: no sentence on the 'Internetwork traffic privacy' page says the path avoids the internet; the FAQ ('bypasses the internet') and remote_regions ('remains on the AWS global network backbone') facts are used instead.

demand.question: The three virtual interface types: private (a VPC through a virtual private gateway or Direct Connect gateway), public (AWS public services by public IP addresses), transit (transit gateways through a Direct Connect gateway). Quote each definition.

Public virtual interface: what it reaches (all AWS public prefixes, for example Amazon S3, in all public Regions), what it does not reach (non-Amazon prefixes, the internet), and whether Direct Connect data transfer out includes transfers to the internet (FAQ).

Direct Connect gateway: a globally available resource; one private virtual interface reaches VPCs in many Regions through it; associates with virtual private gateways or transit gateways; may belong to another account. Can traffic go from one associated VPC to another through it (no)? Can it carry traffic between on-premises sites?

Direct Connect gateway quotas: gateways per account (200), virtual private gateways per Direct Connect gateway (20), transit gateways per Direct Connect gateway (6), private or transit virtual interfaces per Direct Connect gateway (30), Direct Connect gateways per transit gateway (20), prefixes from a transit gateway to on-premises on a transit virtual interface (200). Each row with header and comment.

Routes per BGP session: from on-premises to AWS on a private or transit virtual interface (examinable value 100; the current row adds prefix controls up to 1,000, not examinable yet), on a public virtual interface (1,000). What happens when you advertise more (the BGP session goes idle or down)?

Link aggregation group (LAG): what it is (several dedicated connections as one logical connection, LACP), its rules (same speed, same Direct Connect location, dedicated connections only), maximum members (4 below 100 Gbps; 2 at 100 or 400 Gbps), active/active, minimum links. Does a LAG make the connection more resilient (FAQ)?
LAG quotas: dedicated connections per LAG (row with header), LAGs per Region (10), virtual interfaces per LAG (51).

Resiliency models of the Resiliency Toolkit: maximum resiliency (separate connections on separate devices in more than one location), high resiliency (connections in two locations), development and test (one location, separate devices). Quote what each protects against and the recommendation for critical workloads.
Direct Connect SLA: which availability commitment applies to which configuration (maximum resiliency, high resiliency, single connection)? Quote the SLA page and the whitepaper SLA page.

Site-to-Site VPN as a backup for Direct Connect: can a VPC (virtual private gateway) or a transit gateway use both at once, which path carries traffic while both are up, and what happens when the Direct Connect circuit fails (FAQ items 102 and 135)?
Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD): is asynchronous BFD enabled on the AWS side by default, what are the default detection interval and multiplier, and what must you configure on your router?
Active/active vs active/passive across two Direct Connect connections: local preference BGP communities and AS_PATH prepending; what AWS does by default when no community is set.

SiteLink: what it does (connects on-premises sites through Direct Connect points of presence without passing through a Region), which virtual interfaces support it, the separate fee, the partitions where it is not available, and SiteLink vs AWS Cloud WAN (FAQ).
